newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent to drop unless $19 kept in sight.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent to drop unless $19 kept in sight.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Brent may test the $18.70 and $18.80 highs from last week then the next target would be July 2s $18.96 but will need to close above $19 to reverse the underlying bear sentiment.
* A further block to any upside is a second shorter term downtrend line from May 16's high of $20.60 which caps the market just under $18.60.

Front month Brent crude futures cleared and held above the barrier of the long term downtrend line on Wednesday with the market finishing near the high for the day, but analysts on Thursday were not convinced that the rally will be extended.

The clean break above what has been a fairly tough barrier to brake down could lead to a test of the $18.70 and $18.80 a barrel highs from last week. If these are broken then the next target would be July 2's $18.96 high and the psychological $19 barrier, but they said it would need to break cleanly above $19 to reverse the underlying bear sentiment.
Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Isle of Man said, "We continue to take an overall bearish view of the market, It would take a convincing close above $19 before we change our stance".
He saw initial resistance coming in at $18.79 the high from July 17 on the September chart but thought a test of support at $17.98 was more likely.
"If this breaks we expect the market to maintain the overall trend lower with an initial target of the $17.68 June low and then the longer term 'swing objective' is $16.71, Wilson said.
He explained that the swing objective is derived by subtracting the low from the high of the recent traded range then subtracting the result from the range low.
In this case he takes a range of $18.99 down to $17.85.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International took a similar stance.

"Repeat gains from $17.98 to $18.41 are clearly corrective and very late in development at Wednesday's high," he said. "Fibonacci still offers resistance at $18.48, this implies going back under $17.98 near term and possibly $17.68 in the longer term".

A further block to any upside is a second shorter term downtrend line stemming from May 16's high of $20.60 which currently caps the market just under $18.60 and topped-off the rallies of last Thursday and Friday, analysts said.
Both crude and gas oil momentum indicators remain in neutral to negative mode while slow stochastics which are on a path of convergence that may point the market lower again.

IPE gas oil opened and closed above $162.50 the mid-point of the recently congested period of trade. This happened on Thursday and Friday of last week when the market put in a usually supportive double bottom at $163.25.
Though the second was at the bottom of Friday's traded range and the market opened with a small gap down of around 25 cents on Monday.
Analysts said the significance for Wednesday's break higher was that the market closed near the top of its range with little real resistance until around $168, which may be targeted today.
Nicholas Wilson said "Gas oil paints a similar picture to crude but I expect the rallies to $168 and possibly $169.60 to be kept, though any fall off in crude will drag gas oil lower too".
He said support was in at $160 with a longer term target of around $150.50 depending on the depth of any crude fall.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
